title: The costs of inefficient bargaining and financial distress
authors: Sanjai Bhagat; James A. Brickley; Jeffrey L. Coles
main_finding: UNVERIFIED (abstract not retrieved; summary from general knowledge, check the paper): defendants lose more value at filing than plaintiffs gain, so combined value falls; settlements recover part of the loss.
notes: Bhagat, Brickley & Coles. Daily returns around Wall Street Journal announcements. Metadata verified via Crossref.

title: The Shareholder Wealth Implications of Corporate Lawsuits
authors: Sanjai Bhagat; John Bizjak; Jeffrey L. Coles
case_types: lawsuit filings: environmental, product liability, antitrust, IP, contract, securities
main_finding: UNVERIFIED (abstract not retrieved; summary from general knowledge, check the paper): defendant firms lose about 1% on average when a suit is announced; plaintiffs show no significant gain.
notes: Bhagat, Bizjak & Coles. OpenAlex attached an unrelated abstract to this DOI; ignored. Metadata verified via Crossref.

title: Managerial Opportunism during Corporate Litigation
authors: BRUCE HASLEM
case_types: litigation resolutions: court decisions vs settlements
main_finding: Abstract: for shareholders, a court decision beats a settlement even when the firm loses; the market reads settlement as bad news on average (agency-cost explanation).
notes: Haslem. Metadata verified via Crossref.

title: Patenting in the Shadow of Competitors
authors: Josh Lerner
venue: The Journal of Law and Economics
main_finding: Abstract: biotech firms with high litigation costs avoid patenting in crowded patent subclasses. Not a stock-price event study.
notes: Lerner. Listed because it is often cited with litigation event studies; it measures patenting behaviour, not returns. Metadata verified via Crossref.

title: The Value of Certainty in Intellectual Property Rights: Stock Market Reactions to Patent Litigation.
authors: Alan C. Marco
case_types: patent court decisions (validity/infringement) and patent grants
main_finding: Abstract: resolving validity/infringement uncertainty is worth about as much as the patent grant itself, about 1-1.5% excess return each; reactions differ before/after the 1982 creation of the Federal Circuit; appellate decisions show no extra effect.
notes: Marco. Author calls it the first study of stock reactions to patent-case outcomes. Daily data. Metadata verified via Crossref.

title: The Private Costs of Patent Litigation
authors: James E. Bessen; Michael J. Meurer
main_finding: Abstract: stock-implied cost to defendants is far above legal fees: mean about $28.7M, median $2.9M per suit; infringement risk exceeded 14% of R&D by the late 1990s.
notes: Bessen & Meurer. Metadata verified via Crossref.

title: The effect of Paragraph IV decisions and generic entry before patent expiration on brand pharmaceutical firms
authors: Laura E. Panattoni
case_types: Hatch-Waxman Paragraph IV court decisions (brand drug makers)
sample_size: all Paragraph IV decisions in a hand-built dataset (count not checked)
main_finding: Semantic Scholar summary: Paragraph IV decisions involve the highest-revenue drugs and long remaining patent life. UNVERIFIED (abstract not retrieved; summary from general knowledge, check the paper): brand stock falls on losses at the district court.
notes: Panattoni. Closest prior work to the drug-patent part of this repo. Daily data. Metadata verified via Crossref.

title: The Costs of Conflict Resolution and Financial Distress: Evidence from the Texaco-Pennzoil Litigation
authors: David M. Cutler; Lawrence H. Summers
case_types: single case: Texaco v. Pennzoil (jury verdict, appeals, settlement)
main_finding: Abstract: the dispute cut the two firms' combined value by over $3B; Pennzoil gained one-sixth of what Texaco lost; settlement restored about two-thirds of the loss.
notes: Cutler & Summers. Classic jury-verdict case study. Metadata verified via Crossref.

title: Measuring the Cost of Corporate Litigation: Five Case Studies
authors: Kathleen Engelmann; Bradford Cornell
main_finding: UNVERIFIED (abstract not retrieved; summary from general knowledge, check the paper): case studies find combined shareholder losses far larger than the amounts at stake.
notes: Engelmann & Cornell. Metadata verified via Crossref.

title: On the Determinants and Importance of Punitive Damage Awards
authors: Jonathan M. Karpoff; John R. Lott, Jr.
venue: The Journal of Law and Economics
main_finding: Abstract: argues punitive awards are often unnecessary for contract performance; examines their importance to firms. UNVERIFIED (abstract not retrieved; summary from general knowledge, check the paper): includes an event study of award announcements.
notes: Karpoff & Lott. Metadata verified via Crossref.

title: Shareholder-Initiated Class Action Lawsuits: Shareholder Wealth Effects and Industry Spillovers
authors: Amar Gande; Craig M. Lewis
venue: Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis
main_finding: Abstract: significantly negative reactions to shareholder class actions; part of the loss is priced before filing because investors learn from suits against industry peers.
notes: Gande & Lewis. Metadata verified via Crossref.

title: Horizontal mergers, collusion, and stockholder wealth
authors: B.Espen Eckbo
main_finding: UNVERIFIED (abstract not retrieved; summary from general knowledge, check the paper): rival firms' returns around merger announcements and antitrust challenges do not support the theory that challenged mergers were collusive.
notes: Eckbo. Metadata verified via Crossref.

title: Examining antitrust policy towards horizontal mergers
authors: Robert Stillman
main_finding: UNVERIFIED (abstract not retrieved; summary from general knowledge, check the paper): rivals of challenged merging firms show no significant abnormal returns.
notes: Stillman. Metadata verified via Crossref.

title: Antimerger Policy under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Act: A Reexamination of the Market Power Hypothesis
authors: B. Espen Eckbo; Peggy Wier
venue: The Journal of Law and Economics
case_types: merger challenges after the Hart-Scott-Rodino Act
main_finding: Abstract: tests whether HSR powers helped agencies pick truly anticompetitive mergers to challenge. UNVERIFIED (abstract not retrieved; summary from general knowledge, check the paper): finds little evidence they did.
notes: Eckbo & Wier. Metadata verified via Crossref.

title: Mergers, Antitrust Law Enforcement and Stockholder Returns
authors: James C. Ellert
main_finding: UNVERIFIED (abstract not retrieved; summary from general knowledge, check the paper): merger defendants' stock falls when complaints are filed.
notes: Ellert. Metadata verified via Crossref.

title: Market Reaction to the Filing of Antitrust Suits: An Aggregate and Cross-Sectional Analysis
authors: Kenneth D. Garbade; William L. Silber; Lawrence J. White
venue: The Review of Economics and Statistics
main_finding: UNVERIFIED (abstract not retrieved; summary from general knowledge, check the paper): defendant stock falls when antitrust suits are filed; size of fall varies by case type.
notes: Garbade, Silber & White. Metadata verified via Crossref.

title: The Profitability of Price Fixing: Evidence From Stock Market Reaction to Federal Indictments
authors: Jean-Claude Bosch; E. Woodrow Eckard
venue: The Review of Economics and Statistics
main_finding: UNVERIFIED (abstract not retrieved; summary from general knowledge, check the paper): indicted firms lose value at indictment, implying price fixing was profitable.
notes: Bosch & Eckard. Metadata verified via Crossref.

title: The Effect of EU Antitrust Investigations and Fines on a Firm's Valuation
authors: Luca Aguzzoni; Gregor Langus; Massimo Motta
case_types: EU antitrust: inspections, decisions, court judgments
main_finding: Abstract: a surprise inspection cuts share price 2.89% on average and an infringement decision 3.57%; later EU court judgments have no significant effect.
notes: Aguzzoni et al. Metadata verified via Crossref.

title: The Political Economy of European Merger Control: Evidence using Stock Market Data
authors: Tomaso Duso; Damien J. Neven; Lars‐Hendrik Röller
venue: The Journal of Law and Economics
main_finding: Abstract: uses competitors' stock reactions to judge whether EU merger decisions were right; studies why decisions differ from what the market implies.
notes: Duso, Neven & Roller. Metadata verified via Crossref.

title: Market efficiency in real time
authors: Jeffrey A. Busse; T. Clifton Green
case_types: TV news (CNBC segments) about individual stocks
main_finding: UNVERIFIED (abstract not retrieved; summary from general knowledge, check the paper): prices respond within seconds to a few minutes of on-air reports; positive news is absorbed within about a minute.
notes: Busse & Green. Main reference for intraday speed of public news; not about courts. Metadata verified via Crossref.

title: The intraday speed of adjustment of stock prices to earnings and dividend announcements
authors: James M. Patell; Mark A. Wolfson
case_types: earnings and dividend announcements on the Dow Jones broad tape
main_finding: UNVERIFIED (abstract not retrieved; summary from general knowledge, check the paper): most price adjustment happens within 5-10 minutes of the wire story; some return predictability lasts hours.
notes: Patell & Wolfson. Early transaction-level intraday event study. Metadata verified via Crossref.

title: Run EDGAR Run: SEC Dissemination in a High-Frequency World
authors: JONATHAN L. ROGERS; DOUGLAS J. SKINNER; SARAH L. C. ZECHMAN
case_types: SEC filings (Form 4) feed vs website timing
main_finding: Abstract: most filings reached paying SEC feed (PDS) subscribers before the public website, and that head start was profitable.
notes: Rogers, Skinner & Zechman. Closest analogue to 'primary-source feed before public release'. Metadata verified via Crossref.

title: Trading Against the Random Expiration of Private Information: A Natural Experiment
authors: MOHAMMADREZA BOLANDNAZAR; ROBERT J. JACKSON; WEI JIANG; JOSHUA MITTS
case_types: SEC disclosures released early to some investors
main_finding: Abstract: the SEC accidentally sent disclosures to some investors before the public; trading intensity and price discovery during the early window are studied.
notes: Bolandnazar, Jackson, Jiang & Mitts. Metadata verified via Crossref.

title: The Cost to Firms of Cooking the Books
authors: Jonathan M. Karpoff; D. Scott Lee; Gerald S. Martin
venue: Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis
main_finding: Abstract: legal penalties average $23.5M per firm, while market (reputational) losses are many times larger.
notes: Karpoff, Lee & Martin. Metadata verified via Crossref.

title: Market reaction to patent infringement litigations in the information technology industry
authors: T. S. Raghu; Wonseok Woo; S. B. Mohan; H. Raghav Rao
main_finding: Semantic Scholar summary: defendants' stock falls on suit news; plaintiffs earn positive returns at filing and at settlement/termination.
notes: Raghu et al. Metadata verified via Crossref.

title: Stock Price Response to News of Securities Fraud Litigation: An Analysis of Sequential and Conditional Information
authors: Paul A. Griffin; Joseph A. Grundfest; Michael A. Perino
case_types: securities class actions: filing, corrective disclosure, class-period start
main_finding: Abstract: measures investor response at three dates that define a securities class action. UNVERIFIED (abstract not retrieved; summary from general knowledge, check the paper): most of the loss comes at the corrective disclosure, not the filing.
notes: Griffin, Grundfest & Perino. Metadata verified via Crossref.

title: Law on the Market? Evaluating the Securities Market Impact of Supreme Court Decisions
authors: Daniel Martin Katz; Michael James Bommarito; Tyler Soellinger; James Ming Chen
case_types: US Supreme Court decisions and oral arguments
sample_period: over 15 years (approx. 1999-2013; exact span not checked)
main_finding: Abstract: 79 of 211 cases (37%) show an average 4.4% abnormal return over two sessions; abnormal returns build over hours and days, not minutes.
notes: Katz, Bommarito, Soellinger & Chen. Only verified court-ruling study found that uses intraday prices; SCOTUS decisions are scheduled-day releases, unlike district-court orders. Metadata verified via Crossref.

title: Event Studies and the Law: Part I: Technique and Corporate Litigation
authors: S. Bhagat
case_types: method review: event studies in law
main_finding: Abstract: first of two reviews of how event studies are used in legal settings.
notes: Bhagat & Romano (Crossref lists only Bhagat as author; Roberta Romano is co-author on the article). Metadata verified via Crossref.

title: Dispute the patent, short the stock: Empirical analysis of a new hedge fund strategy
authors: Rabea Kruppert
venue: International Review of Law and Economics
case_types: PTAB inter partes review petitions filed by a hedge fund group against drug patents
main_finding: UNVERIFIED (abstract not retrieved; summary from general knowledge, check the paper): tests whether IPR petitions by the Coalition for Affordable Drugs (Kyle Bass) moved patent owners' stocks; effects mostly small or short-lived.
notes: Kruppert. Only verified PTAB stock-reaction study found; covers petition filings, not PTAB decisions. Metadata verified via Crossref.

title: Using stock price movements to estimate the harm from collusive drug patent litigation settlements
authors: Keith M. Drake; Thomas G. McGuire
main_finding: Abstract: uses stock price movements to estimate consumer harm from collusive brand-generic patent settlements.
notes: Drake & McGuire. Metadata verified via Crossref.

title: The Market Effects of Patent Litigation
authors: Matthew D. Henry
main_finding: Abstract: firms lose 0.85% (about $19M) when a patent is ruled invalid and gain about 0.7% on a valid-and-infringed ruling.
notes: Low-profile journal; treat with care. Metadata verified via Crossref.

title: Are Settlements in Patent Litigation Collusive? Evidence from Paragraph IV Challenges
authors: Eric Helland; Seth Seabury
main_finding: Abstract: studies whether pay-for-delay settlements between brand and generic makers are collusive. UNVERIFIED (abstract not retrieved; summary from general knowledge, check the paper): uses stock reactions to settlement announcements.
notes: NBER working paper. Metadata verified via Crossref.

title: The Shareholder Wealth Effects of Delaware Litigation
authors: Adam B. Badawi; Daniel L. Chen
case_types: Delaware Court of Chancery: derivative suits and merger class actions
main_finding: Abstract: full docket records show how markets respond to Delaware litigation events, by case characteristics such as timing.
notes: Badawi & Chen. Closest prior work to the Delaware deal-litigation part; daily data, docket-level dates. Metadata verified via Crossref.

title: Defendant Cash Holdings in Patent Litigation: The Impact on Shareholder Value
authors: David Tan; Jie Yang
main_finding: UNVERIFIED (abstract not retrieved; summary from general knowledge, check the paper): cash-rich defendants are sued more and lose more at filing.
notes: Tan & Yang. Metadata verified via Crossref.

title: Does the stock market anticipate events and supreme court decisions in corporate cases?
authors: Yehuda Davis; Suresh Govindaraj; Kate Suslava

main_finding: Abstract (SSRN version 3761235): stocks react to cert grants (negative for both sides) and to decisions (winners up, losers down); no evidence of leakage before decisions.
notes: Davis et al. SSRN version matched by title; daily data. Metadata verified via Crossref.

title: Surprise! Most Blockbuster Jury Awards Are Ignored By The Stock Market
authors: Michael Palmer; Thomas B. Sanders
main_finding: Title and abstract: event study of filing and award dates for 17 blockbuster jury awards against public defendants (tobacco excluded); the title's finding is that most awards are ignored by the stock market.
notes: Palmer & Sanders. Metadata verified via Crossref.

title: The impact of patent litigation on shareholder value in the smartphone industry
authors: Sangjun Nam; Changi Nam; Seongcheol Kim
main_finding: Title: impact of patent litigation on shareholder value. UNVERIFIED (abstract not retrieved; summary from general knowledge, check the paper): defendants lose value at filing.
notes: Nam et al. Metadata verified via Crossref.

title: Maintaining the Balance: An Empirical Study on Inter Partes Review Outcomes of Orange Book-Listed Drug Patents and its Effect on Hatch-Waxman Litigation
authors: Tulip Mahaseth

main_finding: Abstract: compares IPR with Hatch-Waxman district-court outcomes for drug patents. Not a stock-price study.
notes: Mahaseth. Useful base rates for PTAB drug cases. Metadata verified via Crossref.

title: Event Study Analysis in Cases with Multiple Brand-Generic Reverse-Payment Settlements
authors: Raymond S. Hartman; Keith M. Drake; Thomas G. McGuire
venue: International Journal of the Economics of Business
main_finding: Abstract: critiques the use of stock event studies to judge whether reverse-payment settlements are anticompetitive.
notes: Hartman et al. Metadata verified via Crossref.

title: Appraisal: Shareholder Remedy or Litigation Arbitrage?
authors: Wei Jiang; Tao Li; Danqing Mei; Randall Thomas
venue: The Journal of Law and Economics
main_finding: Abstract (SSRN 2766776): appraisal petitions rose from 2-3% to about 25% of eligible deals; average annualized gross return to petitioners 32.9% (median 19.3%).
notes: Jiang, Li & Mei. Documented 'litigation arbitrage' strategy. Metadata verified via Crossref.

title: Characteristics of Risk and Return in Risk Arbitrage
authors: Mark Mitchell; Todd Pulvino

main_finding: Abstract: risk arbitrage returns behave like selling index put options: correlated with the market only in sharp sell-offs.
notes: Mitchell & Pulvino. Background on event-driven deal funds. Metadata verified via Crossref.

title: Regulation and welfare: evidence from paragraph IV generic entry in the pharmaceutical industry
authors: Lee Branstetter; Chirantan Chatterjee; Matthew J. Higgins

main_finding: Abstract: early generic entry via Paragraph IV gains consumers $42B and costs producers $32.5B.
notes: Branstetter, Chatterjee & Higgins. Sizes what is at stake in drug-patent rulings. Metadata verified via Crossref.

title: Timing Complex News to Target Attention
authors: Vicente Cuñat; Moqi Groen-Xu

main_finding: Abstract: firms release harder-to-process news when attention is higher, shown with a discontinuity in the US filing system.

title: The effects of news on initial corporate lawsuits
authors: Paul Sergius Koku; Anique A Qureshi; Aigbe Akhigbe
main_finding: Title: effects of news on initial corporate lawsuits. UNVERIFIED (abstract not retrieved; summary from general knowledge, check the paper): defendants fall on first news of a suit.
notes: Koku et al. Metadata verified via Crossref.
